justification: Raise the brief's satellite collection timeout caps so the in-process pure-compute layers stop being killed before they finish. bushfire 10->30, flood 20->50, climate 10->25, terrain 30->55 (CONFIG.timeout_terrain) — matching the standalone-tool budgets. These layers run in the brief's own ThreadPoolExecutor identically to the tools; the only defect was the short caps. Parallel futures return as-soon-as-done so higher caps add no latency unless a layer is genuinely slow.

pre_impl.existing_data: Investigation (agent map): the brief mounts the same FastAPI app as the working tools and calls the same _fetch_* functions in a shared ThreadPoolExecutor; _timed_result(future, cap) collected each satellite layer at 10-30s while the standalone tools allow 55-180s, so flood/terrain/climate timed out and were emitted empty.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The empties read as 'not wired' but the layers actually run in-process — they were just collected too early.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new code or query. Four timeout constants raised; granny left unchanged (it will be decoupled to the working async route next, which also carries the eligibility gate).
pre_impl.external_source_error: Unchanged: a layer that still exceeds its (now higher) cap returns the same NOT_AVAILABLE DataField and the card shows the honest 'couldn't complete' state.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: terrain/flood/climate frequently empty (killed at 10-30s). After: they have the same budget as the standalone tools, so they populate; a genuinely slow/failed layer still degrades to the honest empty state.

values: N/A - timeout constants only, no regulatory values.
queries: N/A - no database or API query added.

break_it.scenario: A satellite layer is genuinely slow or hangs
break_it.what_happens: the brief could wait the full higher cap
break_it.repro: _timed_result still enforces the cap (now 30-55s) and returns NOT_AVAILABLE on timeout
break_it.how: the cap still bounds the wait; parallel collection returns each future as soon as it completes

break_it.scenario: Raising caps serialises the emit and slows the whole brief
break_it.repro: futures are submitted up front and run in parallel; _timed_result returns when the future finishes, not after the full cap
break_it.how: total wait approximates the slowest single layer, not the sum of caps

break_it.repro: granny cap left at 30 intentionally; GF is being decoupled to the gated async route next
break_it.how: GF handled separately; this PR fixes the pure-compute layers only
